display.purpose: The status board's one headline on the index page. Exactly one per site; capped at 22ch with text-wrap: balance.

headline.purpose: Evidence's auto-rendered h1.title on the five deep pages, underlined with a rule-strong hairline and ticked with a 2.5rem caution segment. Hidden on the index via route-scoped CSS.

title.purpose: A module's own name: channel names, the footer byline, the rail wordmark (0.9375rem / 700 / 0.02em).

body.purpose: All running prose, capped at a 68ch measure. Panel's intro slot runs narrower at 62ch.

body-small.purpose: Explanatory copy inside a module: outcome plates, verify cells, coverage and dormant notes.

placard.purpose: The one repeated typographic gesture of the world. Every label on every well, module, step, table header and rail station. Never an eyebrow above a separate heading.

placard-section.purpose: Panel's own h2, cut into an engraved rule. Larger and more tracked than the everyday placard; that difference is the entire hierarchy signal.

readout-lead.purpose: The board's headline figure, one per page at most. Drops to 2.25rem below 640px.

readout.purpose: The standard live value in a well. Channel counts run at 1.25rem, the last-run stamp at 1.125rem.

data.purpose: Every table, inline code span, search input and dbt test name. Tabular figures, always.

fonts.hosting: self-hosted woff2, latin + latin-ext subsets, font-display: swap, declared in dashboard/static/fonts/fonts.css
self-hosted woff2, latin + latin-ext subsets, font-display: swap, declared in dashboard/static/fonts/fonts.css

shadows.name: well-bevel
shadows.purpose: The top lip of a recessed well in the console register. The only shadow in the system, and it is inset — nothing in this world lifts off the page.

shadows.name: well-bevel-daylight
shadows.purpose: The same lip in the daylight register, softened because a printed plot board does not cut as deep as machined metal.

shadows.name: elevation
shadows.purpose: There is no elevation shadow. Depth is four stepped ground values plus two rule weights. Do not add one.

textures.name: panel-machining
textures.value: repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, transparent 0 3px, color-mix(in srgb, var(--rule) 18%, transparent) 3px 4px)
textures.purpose: Faint vertical machining on the console face (.console-shell), at a 4px pitch. Texture, not a pattern anyone should consciously notice.

motion.name: power-on
motion.purpose: The site's ONE authored moment: the status board arriving, 6px rise plus fade. Applied to .board on the index and nowhere else. Adding a second animation breaks the world.

motion.name: ease-state
motion.purpose: The only state transition, on color and border-color: rail stations, the register switch, the primary action, the footer repo plate. Never on transform.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) — .power-on animation: none, plus a global clamp of every animation-duration and transition-duration to 0.01ms !important
motion.purpose: The reduced-motion contract. It is global, not per-component.

layout.frame: max-width: 78rem; margin-inline: auto; padding-inline: 1.5rem (1rem at the narrow breakpoints). Shared identically by the rail, the main content and the footer.
layout.seamGrid: display: grid; gap: 1px; background: var(--rule); border: 1px solid var(--rule) — children strip their own border, border-radius and box-shadow so the group reads as one machined plate subdivided.
layout.measure: 68ch on .markdown p; 62ch on Panel's intro. A full-width paragraph row takes max-width: none on the plate and an inner span.measure at 68ch.

buildInvariants.name: basePath
buildInvariants.note: Required. Evidence 40 does NOT honour EVIDENCE_BASE_PATH; without the config value the GitHub Pages project site returns 200 and renders completely unstyled because every /_app/... request 404s.

buildInvariants.name: themeAttribute
buildInvariants.note: The only valid selector for the daylight register. Evidence sets this attribute and no class and no data-appearance. The rail's own .lamp-switch writes it, because Evidence's built-in switcher lives in the hidden header.

buildInvariants.name: deterministicSort
buildInvariants.value: every ranked query carries a secondary sort key
buildInvariants.note: e.g. `order by posting_count desc, canonical_skill`. Without one, equal-count rows reorder between renders. Two independent renders of the same page are byte-identical by pixel hash after this fix.

buildInvariants.name: directionContract
buildInvariants.note: Svelte strips ordinary HTML comments at compile time, so the contract is raw markup. It is the first HTML comment in every built page and must stay auditable in shipped output.

buildInvariants.name: indexTitleSuppression
buildInvariants.note: Route-scoped on purpose. SvelteKit only loads a route's CSS for that route, which keeps h1.title visible on the five deep pages where it is the station designation. Never move this into console.css.

buildInvariants.name: measuredSurface
buildInvariants.value: six pages, zero horizontal overflow at 1440px and at a true 390px viewport; body contrast 7.5:1 console / 7.4:1 daylight, placards 14-18:1, readouts 15:1; strict production build passes; impeccable detector returns [].

dataviz.assignment: Fixed slot order, never cycled. Slot 1 paints every single-series chart.
dataviz.validation: Validated with the dataviz validator against this world's real grounds (#101619 console panel / #e8ecee plot board), not a generic white. Every check passes in BOTH registers with no warnings: worst adjacent CVD dE 13.0 in both, worst adjacent normal-vision dE 15.5 console / 18.7 daylight.
dataviz.slotOrderRationale: Oxide sand sits between instrument cyan and magenta because those two collide at dE 2.5 under deuteranopia when adjacent. The order IS the CVD-safety mechanism. Do not reorder, insert, drop or resample without re-running the validator against both grounds.
dataviz.slot1Rationale: Slot 1 is a deep instrument cyan and deliberately NOT a blue. A saturated blue in slot 1 is the stock Evidence accent this world's thesis refuses; it made the Skills and Companies plots read as default charts wearing a console frame. Blue is demoted to slot 6, where six concurrent series must be on screen before it appears.
dataviz.reserved: Status hues (nominal green / caution amber / fault red) never appear as a chart series, and instrument-trace hues never appear on a lamp.
dataviz.sequential: One hue, light to dark, cyan to match the categorical lead. Identical in both registers. Never a rainbow.
dataviz.surface: .echarts-wrapper and .chart-container are forced transparent so plots sit in the panel rather than on a white sheet.

narrative.overview:
This is not a dashboard. It is the face of an instrument that ran at 02:30 UTC without a human present, and the single most important thing it has to say is that it is willing to refuse to publish. Every visual decision serves that reading. The surface is a matte console panel machined with faint vertical rules; modules are bolted into its face; live values are sunk into recessed wells; labels are engraved placard capitals cut into hairline rules. Numbers are set in a tabular monospace because a readout is a different kind of object from a sentence, and the two never wear each other's clothes.

The world refuses two opposites at once. It refuses the SaaS-card arrangement Evidence ships by default — sidebar, rounded cards, Inter, a saturated blue accent — which is why the shell hides Evidence's entire chrome and rebuilds the rail, the footer and the type from scratch. It equally refuses the terminal cliche that a "console" invites: there are no scanlines, no glow, no green-on-black, no ASCII art, no blinking cursors. Depth comes from three stepped ground values and hairline rules, never from a drop shadow.

Density is high and deliberately unpadded — this is an operations panel, not a marketing page — but the prose inside it stays at a 68-character measure and reads plainly. The product's voice ("hedges and caveats are content, not clutter to be designed away") is load-bearing on the visual system: caution plates, dormant lamps and "what these numbers do not say" modules are first-class furniture with real estate, not fine print.
keyCharacteristics: Matte console panel with faint vertical machining, three stepped grounds, zero shadows for elevation
Engraved placard capitals (Archivo 600, tracked 0.14em) against tabular readouts (JetBrains Mono)
A single 2px radius everywhere; the corner is a machined chamfer, not a rounded card
Status lamps in exactly three states, reserved for state, never used decoratively or as chart color
Modules separated by 1px seams of rule color, not by gaps
One authored motion moment on the whole site

rules.name: The Reserved Lamp Rule
rules.body: The three status hues exist only to report machine state. They are never a chart series, never a decorative highlight, never a brand gradient. And a lamp never carries meaning in colour alone: StatusLamp always ships an engraved word AND a drawn SVG glyph. Colour is confirmation, not the message.

rules.name: The Slot Order Rule
rules.body: The categorical palette's slot order is a CVD-safety mechanism, not taste. Oxide sand sits between instrument cyan and magenta because those two collide at dE 2.5 under deuteranopia when adjacent. Validated against this world's actual surfaces in both registers with no warnings. Do not reorder, insert, drop or resample a slot without re-running the validator against both grounds.

rules.name: The No Stock Blue Rule
rules.body: Slot 1 is a deep instrument cyan and deliberately not a blue. Slot 1 paints every single-series chart on the site, and a saturated blue there is exactly the stock accent this world's thesis refuses. Blue is demoted to slot 6, where six concurrent series would have to be on screen before it appears.

rules.name: The One-Hue Scale Rule
rules.body: The sequential scale is one hue, light to dark, cyan to match the categorical ramp's lead. It is identical in both registers. Never a rainbow, never a diverging ramp for non-diverging data.

rules.name: The data-theme Rule
rules.body: Light mode is selected on html[data-theme='light'] and nothing else. Evidence sets that attribute and sets no class and no data-appearance; targeting anything else makes the entire daylight register dead code that no switcher can ever reach. The rail's own switch sets the attribute directly, because Evidence's built-in switcher lives in the header this shell hides.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Archivo says what a thing is; JetBrains Mono says how much there is. A number never appears in Archivo, prose never appears in mono, and there is no third face.

rules.name: The Placard-Is-The-Label Rule
rules.body: A placard is the section's own label, never an eyebrow stacked above a separate heading. Panel renders its label as the h2; if you find yourself writing a placard and a heading that say the same thing, delete the heading.

rules.name: The Engraved Identity Rule
rules.body: Nothing identifies itself by colour alone. The active station gets an inset ground and a strong rule border, not a tint. The station designation gets a rule and a tick.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Every paragraph caps at 68ch. When a paragraph is itself a full-width module row with its own background, the plate must span the module (max-width: none) while an inner span.measure keeps the text at 68ch. Two different jobs: uncapping the paragraph alone produces 100-character lines; leaving the cap on ends the row's background mid-module and leaks the container's rule colour through as a phantom cell.

rules.name: The Seam Rule
rules.body: Related modules are separated by a 1px seam of rule colour, never by whitespace and never by a shadow. If two things need to look like part of the same instrument, put them in a seam grid.

rules.name: The Shared Measure Rule
rules.body: Rail, content and footer all sit at 78rem with the same 1.5rem gutter. A new full-width band must adopt both or it will visibly disagree with everything above it.

rules.name: The Three Grounds Rule
rules.body: The daylight register's ground values are stepped further apart than a naive light theme would space them, because the whole 'a module bolted into the console face' reading is carried by that separation. In an earlier tighter light palette the module boundary collapsed to a single 1px rule and the depth story disappeared.

rules.name: The No-Lift Rule
rules.body: Nothing hovers. If something needs to feel prominent, change its ground, its rule weight or its tick colour. Never add a drop shadow, and never add transform: translateY() on hover.

rules.name: The Square Cap Rule
rules.body: Icon strokes end square, not round. A rounded cap softens the instrument and none of the glyphs in the system use one, except the mode-switch crescent, which needs a round join.

dos: Do keep deployment.basePath: /quantyx in evidence.config.yaml. Evidence 40 does NOT honour the EVIDENCE_BASE_PATH environment variable; without the config value the GitHub Pages project site returns 200 and renders completely unstyled, because every /_app/... request 404s. Any asset URL you add must go through base from $app/paths for the same reason.

Do select the daylight register on html[data-theme='light'] and nowhere else, and keep the rail's lamp-switch as the way a visitor reaches it — Evidence's own switcher is in the header this shell hides.

Do give every ranked query a deterministic secondary sort key. Without one, equal-count rows reorder between renders; on a site whose entire thesis is deterministic publishing, that is a correctness defect, not a cosmetic one. Two independent renders of the same page are byte-identical by pixel hash after this fix — keep it that way.

Do hide h1.title with route-scoped CSS on the index only. Evidence auto-renders the frontmatter title into h1.title; on the index the board carries its own headline, so the heading is suppressed inside index.md's own style block. SvelteKit only loads a route's CSS for that route, which is what keeps it off the five deep pages where h1.title is the real station designation. Never move that rule into console.css.
Do give a full-width paragraph row max-width: none on the plate and an inner span.measure at 68ch for the text.
Do ship a word and a glyph with every lamp, and re-run the dataviz validator against both grounds before touching the categorical palette.
Do put new module groups in a 1px seam grid over rule, and strip the child's own border/radius/shadow.
Do state a limit as furniture — a caution plate, a lamp, a dormant note — rather than as small grey text at the bottom.
donts: Don't add a second animation. Motion is exactly one authored moment: a 620ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) power-on applied to .board on the index and nowhere else, disabled under prefers-reduced-motion — which additionally clamps every animation and transition on the site to 0.01ms. State changes get a 140ms ease-out colour/border transition; that is the whole vocabulary.
Don't reorder, resample or extend the categorical palette without re-running the validator. Oxide sand is between cyan and magenta for a reason.
Don't put a status hue on a chart series, and don't put an instrument-trace hue on a lamp.
Don't make slot 1 a blue. Blue is slot 6 and the demotion is the point.
Don't add a drop shadow, a hover lift, a gradient fill or a radius above 2px.

groundTruthNotes: Two inline annotations in dashboard/static/console.css name the wrong ground: --ink-dim is commented '4.9:1 on --panel' (dark) and '7.1:1 on --panel' (light). Recomputed, --ink-dim is ~8.1:1 on --panel in the console register and ~6.2:1 on --panel in daylight; the measured 7.5:1 / 7.4:1 body figures are against --panel-raised, which is where body prose actually sits. The comments understate and misattribute.

TheGate.svelte is named for a GO/NO-GO verdict and the direction contract describes one, but the built component deliberately does not render a live verdict — a build that fails the gate never reaches a browser, so lamps that could only ever read GO would be decoration. It shows which checks are armed plus both outcomes as a worked example. The only genuinely conditional lamp is the volume check, which reads caution/Dormant until seven days of history exist.

The direction contract states the LAST RUN readout sits on the rail; in the built surface the rail carries only the designation, register switch and stations, and the LAST RUN readout lives in the status board's state well immediately below.

The contract embedded in pages/+layout.svelte carries one line the brief's copy does not: 'FINISH: unreviewed and undocumented is unfinished; this build ends with the finish review, the verdict, and DESIGN.md.'
dashboard/app.css is imported by pages/+layout.svelte but does not exist in source; it resolves against Evidence's generated template at dashboard/.evidence/template/src/app.css at build time.

evidence.config.yaml theme.colors.base.light is #e8ecee, a shade lighter than --panel light (#e8ecee). That value is Evidence's own chart ground and the ground the dataviz validator was run against; the console face in daylight is the darker one.
